title: Information- and energy-aware deployment/search planning
description: Joint optimization chooses release positions and search paths for energy-limited UAV teams.
introduction: Where a UAV starts can be as important as the path it follows. This work plans release locations and search trajectories together, using prior target information while accounting for each vehicle’s limited energy and sensing performance.

problem.heading: Spend the search energy where it is useful.
paragraphs: A search area can contain no-fly regions, uncertain target locations and uneven prior information. A vehicle has a finite energy budget, and passing near a location does not guarantee successful detection.

Selecting release locations independently of the search paths can miss useful trade-offs. The starting position determines which promising regions a small UAV can reach and inspect with its remaining energy.

approach.heading: Choose starting points and trajectories together.
paragraphs: The planner receives a target-likelihood map, prohibited regions, vehicle energy budgets and a sensing-performance model. It jointly chooses a release position and search path for each UAV.

Offline simulated-annealing optimization balances search value with travel and sensing constraints. Coordinating the paths helps distribute the team across promising regions while limiting unnecessary overlap.

The publication programme includes the air-dropped multi-UAV planning study and a related information-oriented, energy-aware small-UAV path-planning contribution. Their exact records are listed separately below.

evidence.label: Offline planning example
evidence.text: The presentation illustrates a computed five-UAV deployment and search plan, including prior target likelihood and prohibited regions. It is an offline optimization example, not an actual aerial deployment trial.

evidence.label: Constraint-dependent outcome
evidence.text: The path allocation depends on the specified prior, sensing model and energy budgets. The figures do not establish a general detection probability or hardware endurance result.
